description: This is the fundamental building block for continuous quantities in ENSDF.  It allows additional properties, but ensures that at least a value and some kind of uncertainty are present.

value.description: The central value of approximations and quantities with uncertainties.  In the case of a limit, it is the extreme value of the limit, e.g. the '20' in '<20.'  In the case of a range, it does not have a probabilistic interpretation; it is simply the midpoint between the ends of the range.

evaluatorInput.description: This field is a compatibility aid for tools which may need to read the old string-style values from the database.  Users should expect this field to be removed in the near future.

uncertainty.description: The uncertainty associated with a quantity.  It must always have, at minimum, a 'type.'

anyOf.description: The format for a quantity with symmetric error bars denoting a 1-sigma/68% confidence interval.
The format for a quantity with asymmetric error bars, again describing a 1-sigma/68% confidence limit.
The format for upper and lower limits.
Format for when there is no uncertainty, either because the value is known only approximately, or no uncertainty is reported in a publication.
The format for a range, in which no probability-density function can be associated with a value.  Use this, for example, when two different measurements set limits on a value.
